clue.text: Result of having a six-pack and losing it

definitions.text: Result of having a six-pack and losing it

parts.words: Result of having a six-pack and losing it
parts.note: a six-pack is both a pack of six beer cans and a set of toned stomach muscles; drinking the one loses you the other

explanation.surface: A wry remark about the cost of letting your fitness slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-pack' is read first as toned abdominal muscles; the second reading is six cans of beer, whose drinking builds a paunch where the muscles were.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch built by heavy drinking is the bodily result of too many cans.

clue.text: Turn pale when division changes sides

indicators.note: right becomes left: the letter for right is swapped for the letter for left

parts.note: a branch is a division of a company or organisation

explanation.surface: Someone goes white as their department defects to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes sides' swaps R (right) for L (left) in BRANCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To blanch is to lose colour in the face from shock or fear.

clue.text: Hendrix belief oddly not palatable

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are not taken, so the even ones of Hendrix belief are kept

explanation.surface: Jimi Hendrix's creed is described as hard to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly not' drops the odd letters and keeps the even ones, which spell EDIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is palatable is fit to eat.

clue.text: Murmurs of discontent as empty garages get filled with booze and jewellery

indicators.note: the outside letters are filled by what follows
an empty word keeps only its outer letters, its inside cleared out

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Grumbles arise as cleared-out garages are stuffed with liquor and gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the outside letters of 'garages'; 'get filled with' puts the drink and the jewellery between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling is muttered complaint, so murmured complaints fit.

clue.text: Archer has fooled assembly with a lie

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss marksman who shot an apple off his son's head

indicators.note: an assembly puts the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A political archer is accused of deceiving parliament with an untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges HAS FOOLED A into A FALSEHOOD after TELL. The surface hints at Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and peer jailed for perjury.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying is uttering an untruth, so the phrase is a longer way to say lie.

clue.text: Paul & Co's irregular verbs?

indicators.note: irregular letters are out of their proper order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A grammar question about which verbs Paul and his company conjugate oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges PAUL and COS. Copulas are linking verbs, and 'to be', the chief one, is irregular, so the definition and indicator interlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A copula is a linking verb such as 'is' joining subject and complement.

clue.text: Stop skirting the issue of top ethnic Me Too movement

indicators.note: letters set in movement are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An appeal to stop evading questions about the leading ethnic voices in the Me Too campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like the campaign's own label, but it signals rearranging TOP ETHNIC ME TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the heart of a matter is to stop beating about the bush.

clue.text: 15s food

definitions.meaning: plural of the answer at 15, untruths; this is Cockney rhyming slang (meat pastries rhyme with the word for untruths)
a kind of savoury pastry filled with meat

explanation.walkthrough: 15 is FALSEHOOD, so '15s' means lies. Cockney rhyming slang, a London code, uses a pair of words rhyming with the meant word: here porky pastries for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the pastries stand for lies; literally they are a cold British snack of pork in pastry.

clue.text: Be a remainer? That's pants

parts.note: to linger is to remain behind
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on being a Remain voter in the Brexit vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remainer' points to Brexit politics; here it simply means one who stays on. 'pants' is British slang for rubbish but also British for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain pants are underpants, so women's underwear generally suits it.

clue.text: Yell, perhaps, or be quiet, sweetest heart: if air is air and sea is sea …

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle two letters

parts.words: if air is air and sea is sea
parts.note: the pattern continues to the third element, so ground follows as 'land is land'

explanation.surface: A lover's poetic plea to hush, built on a chain of elemental truisms.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots invite completing the sequence: air is air, sea is sea, so land is land. Yell is one of the Shetland Isles, off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Yell is one member of the Shetland group, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Gold-plated cube is so long

indicators.note: a plated object is coated, so the gold wraps round the cube

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a small numbered cube used in games

explanation.surface: A gilded die is described as something farewell-ish, a cryptic jumble of a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold-plated' reads as one adjective, but it splits: the gold symbol coats, or is 'plated' round, the cube.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual ways to say goodbye; the French farewell is used in English.

clue.text: Most recent concoction after fruit crush

indicators.note: this mixture follows the fruit in the answer

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are blended anew
most of the word, not all: the final letter is left off

explanation.surface: A recipe step: blend a fresh mixture once the fruit is crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' drops the last letter of 'recent', 'concoction' rearranges what is left, and 'after' sets it behind the fruit. 'crush' looks like a cooking verb but is the noun for a passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Limerence is the obsessive state of being in love with someone, i.e. having a romantic crush.

clue.text: Worshippers' bathing ritual starts with immersion in cleanest fluid

definitions.note: the clue gives a possessive plural; the answer is the plain plural

indicators.note: the opening letters are dipped into the rearranged letters
fluid letters are not fixed and flow into a new order
the starts of these two words give their opening letters

explanation.surface: A congregation's ritual of baptism by full immersion in the purest water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the opening letters of 'bathing ritual'; 'fluid' rearranges 'cleanest'; 'with immersion in' dips the first pair into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrants are those who take part in a religious rite, so they are people at worship.

clue.text: Like a good dog in spring, I daren't go barking

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy

explanation.surface: A dog, out for a spring walk, decides against barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for mad, short for 'barking mad'; 'go barking' rearranges I DARENT into TRAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A good dog is obedient, having been taught its commands properly.

clue.text: Exposed tax-averse rider

parts.note: the legend of the Coventry noblewoman who rode naked through the town so her husband would lift a harsh tax

explanation.walkthrough: The legend says she rode naked through Coventry, an English city, to make her husband cancel a tax; the clue reads like a headline about a tax dodger.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend makes the eleventh-century countess a nude horsewoman protesting taxation.

clue.text: How to fry tuna? Add endless oil and stir for 10

parts.note: food is fried in fat

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters into a new order
without its end, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A cooking tip for frying tuna, with oil to be added and stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts OIL to OI; 'stir' rearranges TUNA and OI into UATION. 10 is LIMERENCE, a crush.
explanation.definitionFit: An infatuation is a short-lived intense passion, the same thing as a crush.

clue.text: See 4
Hang for having shotgun in part of Las Vegas

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go into the boulevard

parts.note: the Strip is the famous casino boulevard in Las Vegas

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so the letters of gun are scrambled

explanation.surface: Lynching someone for carrying a gun on the Vegas boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shotgun' splits in two: 'shot' scrambles 'gun', and 'in' puts the result inside the boulevard name.
explanation.definitionFit: To lynch or hang someone is to suspend them by the neck from a rope.

clue.text: Perfectionist finding swab originally left inside heart

indicators.note: originally means at its origin, the first letter
left is placed inside the heart word

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A fussy surgeon left a swab inside a patient's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives S; 'inside' puts L in TICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact standards, so a perfectionist is one.

clue.text: Are all Getty items to be moved into an alternative suitable location?

indicators.note: the letters of the words are items that need moving into another order

explanation.surface: Asks if the Getty museum's collection should be rehoused somewhere fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'items to be moved' rearranges ARE ALL GETTY. The Getty is a Los Angeles art museum; the Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A London art museum would be a fitting alternative home for a collection of paintings.

clue.text: Inside job I'd denied, as ordered

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A suspect denies an inside job, as instructed by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside job' reads as crime slang, but 'Inside' signals the letters within 'job I'd denied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidden is an old past participle of bid, meaning commanded or instructed.

clue.text: See 8
Short distance from born-again Christian

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tiny gap separates someone from an evangelical believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to letters within 'born-again Christian'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small unit of length, under three centimetres.

clue.text: What Federer might earn after tax and expenses

definitions.text: What Federer might earn after tax and expenses

parts.words: What Federer might earn after tax and expenses
parts.note: earnings after deductions, with a nod to the tennis star's game played over the net

explanation.walkthrough: Roger Federer is a tennis champion; the clue reads as accountancy until the tennis net comes to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Take-home income once costs and tax are deducted is the accountant's term for earnings left over.

clue.text: See 5
See 6
Battle nerve is to bandage cut in retreat

parts.note: gall means cheek or nerve

indicators.note: the two letters wrap round the next piece as a bandage wraps a wound

parts.note: jocular: 'is' read as the plural of the letter I, giving two I's

indicators.note: going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A wounded soldier's nerve holds as he dresses a cut during a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is read jokily as the plural of the letter I, two I's; 'to bandage' wraps them round the word for cut, which 'in retreat' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1915 Dardanelles campaign in Turkey is known as the battle of that name.

clue.text: Country hotel takes precedence

definitions.meaning: in the NATO alphabet, Hotel (H) comes immediately before the code word for I

explanation.walkthrough: The radio alphabet runs Golf, Hotel, India: so India is the one that Hotel precedes.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Asian republic is also the radio code word for I.

clue.text: Unexpected departures artlessly scanned

indicators.note: unexpected letters land in a surprising new order
the word read as art-less: without art, so those letters go

explanation.surface: Surprise exits are clumsily noted on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artlessly' splits as art-less: 'departures' loses ART, leaving DEPURES, and 'Unexpected' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read through, so the past tense means read or scanned.
